conviction_note: The base case is a beat of the guided top end, as in Q2: revenue $299.0m against a $285.5m guide top. Against that sit three things: the name sold three of its last four beat-and-raise prints, the direct counterparty (Shopify international GMV +32% in Q3 against +37% in Q2) and Mastercard's card-not-present cross-border series both slowed in Q3, and the street's Q4/FY numbers already sit at or above the guide. That gives a mild down lean, p_up 46, on a large two-sided move of abs 11. The findings sum to -2.8 against the scaled -0.9 because the findings carry every lean at full size, while p_up only shades a coin flip on a name whose last four reactions run from -8.9% to +17%.

findings.finding: Global-e has beaten its own guided top end by a wide margin: Q2 2026 revenue was $299.0m against a $278.5-285.5m guide (+6% vs the midpoint, +4.7% vs the top) and GMV $2,089m (+44%) against $1,945-1,985m. Its Q3 guide implies GMV +34% (midpoint $2,020m against Q3 2025's $1,512m), a 10-point deceleration from Q2 that Passport (about $20m of Q3 GMV) barely changes. A repeat of the Q2 pattern gives revenue of about $325-330m against a street of $313-319m and a guide top of $315.5m. On 2026-08-12 the company also cited 'continued strong volume trends from both existing and recently launched merchants', six weeks into Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Every recent quarter printed at or above the guide top, and the reactions were mixed: Q3 2025 -5.1% pre-market on a beat and raise; Q4 2025 +17% (first FY guide); Q1 2026 gapped down to about $27.8 (baseline -8.9%) on a beat and raise; Q2 2026 -0.9% after +15% intraday.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: consensus already sits at or above the guide top, so a beat of the top is the base case. The unpriced part is the size. If the market expected a Q2-sized beat (~$330m), the published consensus would sit near $325m rather than $313-319m.
findings.independence: Q2 beat size against guide from the Q1 call transcript (Q2 guide GMV $1.945-1.985bn, revenue $278.5-285.5m): https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/13/global-e-glbe-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/ . Q3 2025 GMV of $1,512m 'at or above the top end of guidance': https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/global-e-reports-third-quarter-2025-results-2025-11-19

findings.finding: Shopify, Global-e's largest channel (Managed Markets runs on Global-e as merchant of record), reported Q3 2026 on 2026-11-03 after Global-e last spoke. International GMV grew 32% against 37% in Q2, Europe slowed to 33% from 34% (42% a year earlier), and total GMV of $119.1bn (+29%) and revenue missed consensus. SHOP fell about 7%.
findings.link: Shopify Managed Markets uses Global-e as the merchant of record (Canada/UK added July 2026, https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/shopify-managed-markets-now-available-in-canada-and-the-uk). Shopify holds a Global-e stake valued at $879m at Q3 end (ppc.land). The share of Global-e GMV coming through Shopify is not sourced here.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced instance of GLBE reacting to a Shopify GMV print found.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: GLBE is down about 5% since 2026-11-09. Global-e's own Q3 guide already assumes a 10-point GMV slowdown (44% to 34%), bigger than Shopify's 5-point international slowdown, so the counterparty data argues for a smaller beat, not a miss. A fully priced read would show GLBE consensus revisions down after 2026-11-03, and none was found.
findings.independence: Shopify miss and -7% reaction: https://techbuzz.ai/articles/shopify-tumbles-7-on-q3-revenue-gmv-miss-despite-earnings-beat . Q2 international +37%: search snippet citing https://www.digitalcommerce360.com/article/shopify-revenue-gmv/ . Net of the rest of the company: Global-e's enterprise and direct merchants and Passport (~$24-26m of Q3 revenue) are outside this signal.

findings.finding: Mastercard's Q3 2026 cross-border card-not-present volume excluding travel grew 15% against 20% in Q2, and total cross-border volume grew 11% against 12%. The CFO attributed the slowdown to a new EU customs fee, the timing of large retail promotions and lower crypto purchases.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a macro proxy, and the reasons Mastercard gives (intra-Europe, crypto) are mostly not Global-e's flows. Few GLBE previews cite card-network cross-border data.
findings.independence: Proxy only. Points the same way as the Shopify international slowdown (finding 2), from a different source.

findings.finding: Reaction function: Global-e sold three of its last four beat-and-raise prints. Q3 2025 (2025-11-19) fell 5.1% pre-market despite results at or above the guide top and a FY raise. Q1 2026 (2026-05-13) gapped down (baseline -8.9%) on EPS of $0.27 against $0.18 and a FY raise. Q2 2026 (2026-08-12) reversed from +15% intraday to about -0.9%. The exception is Q4 2025 (+17%, first FY guide).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This finding is the reaction history: -5.1% (pre-market), +17%, -8.9%, -0.9% over the last four prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the put skew (+6) and the slightly bearish sentiment EW reports reflect it. If the market expected a sell-off on a beat, the stock would have weakened into the print, and it is -4% over 5 days. So this is partly in the price.

findings.finding: The stock comes in lower, not stretched: $40.32 against $42.49 on 2026-11-09 (-5%), -4.0% over 5 days and -3.5% over 20, about 18% below the mean analyst target ($47.6-49.3), and EW calls sentiment 'still slightly bearish'. The bar is not inflated by a run-up.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025 (+17%) came after a weak tape. Q2 2026 came after the stock rose into the print (CEO sales at $41.23 on 2026-08-04) and reversed. Pattern suggestive, not established.
findings.why_not_priced: By definition this is in the price. It matters for the reaction because a pre-print give-back lowers the real bar. A stock priced for a big beat would be at or above its year high going in, and it is 10% below the 52-week high.
findings.independence: Baseline tape (run_up_5d -3.98%, pct_from_52w_high -10.26%). Benzinga target average $47.6: https://www.benzinga.com/quote/GLBE/analyst-ratings

findings.finding: Next guide: the FY2026 guide midpoint ($1,330m revenue) implies Q4 revenue of about $467m, while the street sits at about $472.6m for Q4 and $1.34bn for FY. A raise that only passes the Q3 beat through therefore leaves Q4 at or below the street, the setup that was sold in Q3 2025 (Q4 GMV guide $2,195-2,315m) and Q1 2026. The holiday quarter is the largest (Q4 2025 revenue $337m), so the Q4 guide carries the reaction.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: Q4 guide plus FY raise, -5.1% pre-market. Q4 2025: first FY guide calling for acceleration to about 30% growth, +17%. The guide line moves this stock the most in both directions.
findings.why_not_priced: The street's Q4 figure (Yahoo, about $472.6m) already sits above the implied guide, so the market expects more than a flow-through raise. If it were priced for a flow-through only, the Q4 consensus would sit near $467m.
findings.independence: Street FY $1.34bn (range $1.32-1.35bn) and Q4 $472.6m: search snippet of https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/GLBE/analysis/ (single aggregator, flagged as possibly inconsistent). Q3 2025 guide pattern: https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/global-e-reports-third-quarter-2025-results-2025-11-19

findings.finding: Margin quality: non-GAAP gross margin fell to 45.3% in Q2 from 46.5% a year earlier, on Passport's mid-30s gross margin, the Managed Markets V2 migration (which recognizes only Global-e's share of the fee and lowers the reported take rate) and absorbed fuel surcharges. The Q3 adj. EBITDA guide ($58.5-62.5m) implies a margin of about 19.3% at the midpoint, against 20.9% in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026's drop was attributed in part to negative free cash flow (MarketBeat). The Q2 reversal was attributed to Passport margin dilution and valuation (business-news-today). Not cleanly isolated.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the dilution was guided and is flagged in previews. The unpriced part is whether gross margin steps down again with the first full Passport quarter. The EPS whisper of $0.35 above a $0.23-0.33 consensus suggests the buy side expects profit upside, not further dilution.
findings.independence: Gross margin 45.3% vs 46.5% and Passport Q3 EBITDA under $1m: Q2 6-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001835963/000117891326004050/exhibit_99-1.htm (shares a document with finding 1). MM V2 take-rate mechanics: Q1 call https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/13/global-e-glbe-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/

findings.finding: Shopify Managed Markets dropped DDU (duties unpaid) support from 2026-08-24: every Managed Markets market that supports DDP moved to duties-and-taxes-collected-at-checkout, with Global-e as merchant of record. The only opt-out was to turn Managed Markets off for that market. This moves more Managed Markets orders onto Global-e's full DDP flow for the last five weeks of Q3.
findings.link: Shopify Managed Markets is operated with Global-e as merchant of record. The change applies only to Managed Markets merchants.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a merchant-facing changelog item that no GLBE preview mentions. The direction for Global-e's revenue is unquantified: merchants turning off Managed Markets would cut volume, while DDP orders lift the duty/FX economics. If it were priced, an analyst would have quantified it, and none was found.
findings.independence: Secondary blog citing Shopify's 2026-08-11 changelog. No second source confirms the volume effect.

findings.finding: Short interest built into the print: 3.85m shares (2.29%) on 2026-09-30 rose to 4.88m (2.90%, 3.6 days to cover) on 2026-10-30, up 27% in a month. Combined with a +6 put skew, positioning leans mildly bearish, but the level is too low for a squeeze to be a mechanism.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price. This item is filed so the judges see that shorts were adding, not covering, into the print.
findings.independence: Baseline skew_25d +6.06 and put/call OI 1.15 (sealed baseline).

findings.why_not_priced: The authorization is known. The Q3 pace is not, but it is a small line for this stock.

baseline_tension: The evidence agrees with the +6 put skew and the downside-paid lean (a counterparty slowdown, a name that sells its beats, a street already above the implied Q4), but the stock has already given back about 5% into the print, so the lean is kept mild (p_up 46) rather than following the skew all the way.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (a narrow proxy is filed small): the Mastercard cross-border series went from -0.5 to -0.3, because the CFO's stated causes (intra-Europe EU customs fee, crypto) are mostly not Global-e flows.
Lesson 1 / core table (this name sells its beats): applied once, through the reaction-history finding (-1.5). The consensus-bar finding was not shrunk a second time.
